Audio / ESP32 / reverse engineering

Active Speakers ESP32 Controller

A volume/input controller for Hypex-based active speakers, built around the awkward fact that a good audio system is still a system: analogue levels, digital transport, balanced outputs, input selection, mute state and a USB protocol that was not designed to be charming.

Signal chain

The useful version of the diagram.

Vinyl through preamp and miniDSP, out over Toslink to a Topping DX5 II, then balanced XLR into the Hypex FA503 modules. The miniDSP establishes the ADC/DSP sample rate, the DX5 II acts as DAC and preamp, and the Hypex modules still have their own input, volume and mute state. That is the kind of diagram that looks simple until it goes quiet.

Debugging

When silence is still a signal.

The Topping could show healthy input levels while the room remained silent, which means the problem was downstream of the digital input. The useful tests were boring in the best way: play a fixed tone, measure XLR pins 2 and 3 for AC voltage, try RCA into the Hypex, explicitly select the Hypex input, then check mute and gain instead of assuming the amplifier was broken.

Controller

The ESP32 bit.

The controller work came from reverse-engineering the Hypex USB protocol with Wireshark, then building something physical to drive volume and source selection. It sits somewhere between hi-fi, embedded systems, and the special kind of stubbornness caused by wanting a proper knob.

Hardware choices

Balanced when it matters.

A lot of the surrounding work was choosing the boringly-correct bits: balanced XLR where possible, short RCA where not, line-level conversion rather than mystery audio boxes, and a neat controller connection that could use USB-C on the box while talking to the Hypex Mini-USB port.

Active Speakers ESP32 Controller Hypex, miniDSP, Topping, XLR and a proper knob.
